headline: I build cloud infrastructure *as code* — and the pipelines that *ship* it.
intro: Computer Science & AI graduate and cloud engineer. I build on AWS across compute, serverless, networking and IAM, containerise with Docker and Kubernetes, run keyless CI/CD in GitHub Actions, and define it all in Terraform, CloudFormation and SAM.

stats.label: uptime on my NTI AWS build

chaptersIntro: From a single line of code to infrastructure across the cloud — scroll through how I got here.

chapters.title: It started with code
chapters.body: I began a B.Sc. in Computer Science & Artificial Intelligence at Capital University in Cairo — and quickly cared less about code running on my machine than about code running reliably everywhere.

chapters.title: My first AWS architecture
chapters.body: Through the NTI program I designed a segmented VPC with public and private subnets, and ran a highly available EC2 web app with assets on S3 — 99.9% uptime, CloudWatch alerting and disaster recovery proven by failover tests.

chapters.title: Everything as code
chapters.body: I built a serverless URL shortener from 25+ resources in AWS SAM and CloudFormation, deploying in under two minutes through keyless GitHub Actions CI/CD — OIDC to short-lived IAM roles, no stored credentials.

chapters.title: Systems under real load
chapters.body: For my graduation project I engineered a hybrid intrusion detection system: Redis Pub/Sub services, a FastAPI and PostgreSQL backend and an ML-plus-Snort pipeline sustaining ~111K flows per second, all containerised. Meanwhile I ran Microsoft 365 and first-line IT as an intern at Genesis Creations.

chapters.title: GitOps, and what's next
chapters.body: Today I'm building a GitOps lab — Terraform-provisioned AWS and a k3s cluster whose state ArgoCD reconciles straight from Git — while preparing for AWS Solutions Architect – Associate. Next: a DevOps or Cloud Engineering role, on-site, hybrid or remote.
